Relevant Article Text: The generally recognized clinical presentations are as follows: the complete form, involving all three major symptoms; the incomplete form, with periostosis but without pachydermia; and the forme frustra with pachydermia and minimal or no skeletal anomalies.   Both forms are autosomal dominant with incomplete penetrance and recessive inheritance has been suggested.1---4 It begins during childhood or adolescence and progresses gradually over the next ﬁve to 20 years before stabilizing.3 The pathogenesis of PDP is still not clearly understood.
